I can spot a claim attributed to nobody.
I can avoid concealment in my own writing.

p.text: What does Aziz say to do when you cannot name the owner?
options: Ask the office who first said it
Drop the claim; you never had it
Keep it and mark it as your own
Put it into a note at the foot

fb.correct: 'Name the owner or drop the claim.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'Name the owner or drop the claim.'

1.say: 'There was a failure of oversight.' Who failed? It does not say. Turn that noun back into a verb and you will see what the sentence is hiding. Somebody did not check something. 'The district did not check the figures for two years.' Now there is a person, an action and a date. The first version has none of the three. It is in every report I have ever read. Because it is comfortable. Nobody is accused and nothing is denied. There is another line. 'It is widely believed that the bridge is safe.' Believed by whom? It does not say that either. Widely, generally, some say, it is thought. Every one of them is a claim with the owner taken off it. How do I fix it? Name the owner or drop the claim. If you can do neither, you never had the claim in the first place.

grammar.label: nominalisation as concealment
grammar.form: turning a verb with an agent into a noun with none
grammar.meaning: removes who did what while appearing to describe it

explanation.en: 'There was a failure of oversight' replaces 'nobody checked'. The noun has no subject, so no one is named, and the sentence sounds more serious while saying less. This is the single most reliable marker of institutional evasion in English, and spotting it is a reading skill before it is a writing one.
explanation.uz: 'There was a failure of oversight' — 'hech kim tekshirmadi' o'rniga. Otda ega yo'q, demak hech kim nomlanmaydi. Bu ingliz rasmiy tilidagi eng ishonchli qochish belgisi.

grammar.positive_example: There was a failure of oversight. Nobody checked the second copy.
grammar.negative_example: There was a failure of oversight, and lessons will be learned going forward.

l1_notes.uz: Ot shakliga o'tkazish ingliz rasmiy tilida juda keng tarqalgan; tarjimada mas'uliyatning yo'qolishi sezilmaydi.

grammar.label: weasel words and the unattributed claim
grammar.form: it is widely believed; some say; critics argue; studies show
grammar.meaning: attributes a claim to nobody in particular, so nobody can check it

explanation.en: 'Studies show' without a citation is the written form of a shrug. The construction survives because it is useful: it lends the authority of evidence without the cost of producing any. Its opposite is not always a footnote — sometimes it is simply naming who says it and letting the reader weigh them.
explanation.uz: 'Studies show' — iqtibossiz bo'lsa, bu yozma yelka qisish. Qurilma foydali bo'lgani uchun yashab qoladi: dalil obro'sini beradi, dalil keltirish xarajatisiz.

grammar.positive_example: Two studies show it, both funded by the applicant, and I have named them.
grammar.negative_example: Studies show it, and it is widely believed by most experts in the field.

l1_notes.uz: Manbasiz da'vo ingliz jurnalistikasida keng tarqalgan; uni sezish tanqidiy o'qish mahorati.

story.title: There was a failure of oversight

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Turn that noun back into a verb and you will see what the sentence is hiding. Somebody did not check something.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: 'The district did not check the figures for two years.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Now there is a person, an action and a date. The first version has none of the three.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: It is in every report I have ever read.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Because it is comfortable. Nobody is accused and nothing is denied.

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: There is another line. 'It is widely believed that the bridge is safe.'

body.speaker: Dilnoza
body.text: It does not say that either.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Widely, generally, some say, it is thought. Every one of them is a claim with the owner taken off it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Name the owner or drop the claim. If you can do neither, you never had the claim in the first place.
